title: Open-source serving stacks ship signed-checkpoint loading as default by Q4 2026
body: By Q4 2026 the Tuesday serving-tier and local-LLM-stack adoption of the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft joint signed-checkpoint reference implementation forces the open-source inference-serving cohort — vLLM, SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and Ray Serve — to ship signature-verified model-checkpoint loading as the documented default load path at the serving tier rather than as an opt-in feature. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and mutually reinforcing: vLLM v0.11.3 ships a Tuesday point release adding a Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature-verified model-checkpoint loader and becomes the first open-source serving stack to ship the signed-checkpoint primitive at the serving tier; Unsloth ships the same primitive at the local-LLM fine-tuning stack tier on the same day, the first local-LLM stack to do so ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target; the Cloudflare Infire production-deployment note reports the new loader plus the tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode close the L40S edge-tier latency gap to a 1.18x Infire advantage (down from 1.25x at the v0.11.2 Monday checkpoint) with a parity-window targeted at v0.11.4 in late-May; the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh places vLLM v0.11.3 at approximately 16,580 tok/s on the shared-prefix workload versus 18,140 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.6, narrowing the throughput gap to 9.4 percent from 11.3 percent Monday; and the Tuesday DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft joint follow-up preprint (arxiv 2605.06712) extends the Monday signed-checkpoint format to cover the inference-routing tier and explicitly anchors the runtime-verifier integration pattern to vLLM, SGLang, TGI, and TensorRT-LLM as the reference serving stacks. The structural force is that once one production-tier serving stack ships signature-verified loading on the same day a leading local-LLM fine-tuning stack ships the matching primitive, and the runtime-verifier preprint anchors the cohort with named reference implementations, the remaining serving-tier maintainers cannot leave unsigned checkpoint loading as the documented default while the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema and the CISA KEV cadence treat signed-load posture as paired procurement-eligibility evidence; the convergence of the vLLM-SGLang throughput gap to single digits removes the last performance argument for postponing the change. The most likely shape is the signed-checkpoint loader becoming the default load path in the next minor release of SGLang RadixArk, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and Ray Serve, with an explicit unsigned-load opt-out flag for sandboxed test fixtures and reproduction harnesses; sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate serving tenants adopt the loader first because the Indo-Pacific eleven-jurisdiction cohort plus the AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex agent-registry public-preview interop already exposes signed-load posture as a tenant-policy field. Bear case is that one serving stack forks the loader contract or ships a sandbox-only mitigation; absent that, Q4 2026 lands signature-verified model-checkpoint loading as the documented default at the serving tier across the open-source cohort.

reasoning.because: Tuesday vLLM v0.11.3 + Unsloth ship signed-checkpoint loader same day; runtime-verifier preprint.
reasoning.given: vLLM-SGLang throughput gap narrows to 9.4% and reciprocity attestation needs signed-load evidence.
reasoning.so_that: SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, and Ray Serve ship signature-verified loading as the documented default load path.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; open-source serving cohort; sovereign-cloud tenants first.
reasoning.plain_language: AI servers will soon refuse to load model files unless they are digitally signed, like apps on a phone.

summary: vLLM v0.11.3 ships a Tuesday signed-checkpoint loader as the first open-source serving stack; Unsloth ships the matching primitive at the local-LLM tier the same day. By Q4 2026 signature-verified checkpoint loading lands as the default load path across the open-source serving cohort.
